translationRepairs: On the eve of resigning he sent a long letter to Grand Councilor Wang. It began: "The emperor's hunger for reform is keen and the empire's longing for order still keener, yet the machinery of government has barely moved. The reasons, I believe, are several.

On the eve of resigning he sent a long letter to the Grand Council prince-ministers. It began: "The emperor's hunger for reform is keen and the empire's longing for order still keener, yet the machinery of government has barely moved. The reasons, I believe, are several.
軍機王大臣 means the prince-minister(s) of the Grand Council (王大臣), not a person surnamed Wang.

About to request leave and return home, he submitted a letter to the Grand Council minister Wang stating his views, in summary as follows: "Today the Son of Heaven's desire for good government is urgent, and the empire's longing for good government is exceedingly pressing, yet the machinery of state has not turned—tracing the causes, there are several.

About to request leave and return home, he submitted a letter to the Grand Council prince-ministers stating his views, in summary as follows: "Today the Son of Heaven's desire for good government is urgent, and the empire's longing for good government is exceedingly pressing, yet the machinery of state has not turned—tracing the causes, there are several.
軍機王大臣 is an office designation for princely Grand Council ministers, not "minister Wang".

In the early Qianlong years the emperor labored from dawn to midnight in pursuit of perfect government. Men such as E Zhun, Zhu Shi, Zhang Tingyu, and Sun Jiagan spoke plainly and styled themselves seasoned mentors of the throne.

In the early Qianlong years the emperor labored from dawn to midnight in pursuit of perfect government. Men such as E Wenduan, Zhu Wenduan, Zhang Wenhe, and Sun Wending spoke plainly and styled themselves seasoned mentors of the throne.
鄂文端 is the posthumous name Wenduan (not "E Zhun"); the paired forms 硃文端、張文和、孫文定 should likewise keep the posthumous-name readings used in the Chinese.
Fortunately since Your Majesty took personal rule, Li Fenghan has died, Zheng Yuanhong has been impeached, Fu Gang has left office in mourning, and Jiang Lan has been transferred inland.
Fortunately since Your Majesty took personal rule, Li Fenghan has died, Zheng Yuanshuang has been impeached, Fu Gang has left office in mourning, and Jiang Lan has been transferred inland.
The given name 鸘 is read shuang, not hong; idiomatic Zheng Yuanhong mistransliterates 鄭元鸘.

Fortunately since Your Majesty's personal rule, Li Fenghan has already died by himself, Zheng Yuanhong has already been impeached, Fu Gang has already suffered bereavement, Jiang Lan has already been transferred within.

Fortunately since Your Majesty's personal rule, Li Fenghan has already died by himself, Zheng Yuanshuang has already been impeached, Fu Gang has already suffered bereavement, Jiang Lan has already been transferred within.
The given name 鸘 is read shuang, not hong; literal Zheng Yuanhong mistransliterates 鄭元鸘.
When I was in the inner court, a colleague told me: 'Of us ten princes, six or seven already keep vegetarian fasts and abstain from killing—sheep, pigs, geese, and ducks never enter our doors.'
When I was in the inner court, colleagues told me: 'Of us ten princes, six or seven already keep vegetarian fasts and abstain from killing—sheep, pigs, geese, and ducks never enter our doors.'
Chinese 執事曾告之曰 is plural colleagues speaking as 某等; idiomatic singular a colleague understates the source.
Hubei and northern Huguang to Governor-General Bi Yuan and Grand Coordinator Wang Xin.
Northern Chu to Governor-General Bi Yuan and Grand Coordinator Wang Xin.
楚北 means northern Chu/Hubei; the idiomatic rendering invents an extra Huguang region not present in the Chinese.
The evidence is already exposed. Even if inner eunuchs lent their influence, these men's concealment and bungling are plainer still.
The evidence is already exposed. Even if inner court ministers lent their influence, these men's concealment and bungling are plainer still.
內臣 means inner-court ministers/officials, not specifically eunuchs; the idiomatic translation mistranslates the term.
Lady Qi of Wang, Yao Zhifu at Xiangyang, Tan Jiayao and Zhang Zhengmo at Changyang, and others took up arms on the news, and the revolt spread into Henan and Shaanxi.
Qi Wangshi (Wang, née Qi) and Yao Zhifu of Xiangyang, and Tan Jiayao, Zhang Zhengmo, and others of Changyang, took up arms on the news, and the revolt spread into Henan and Shaanxi.
齊王氏 is Wang of the Qi family (Wang, née Qi), not “Lady Qi of Wang”; the idiomatic phrasing reverses the name structure.
I ask that Grand Coordinator Le Bao be ordered to investigate strictly and report for punishment.
I ask that Military Commissioner Le Bao be ordered to investigate strictly and report for punishment.
經略 denotes a military commissioner, not Grand Coordinator (巡撫).
He should be ordered through Grand Coordinator Le Bao to investigate strictly and report for disposition.
He should be ordered through Military Commissioner Le Bao to investigate strictly and report for disposition.
Same mistranslation of 經略 as Grand Coordinator in the literal English.

Moreover, an imperial grace decree now commands that all who accept pacification and return be ordered through Le Bao to summon Subprefect Liu Qing, together with Sichuan prefects and magistrates of long-standing clean reputation, to deliberate proper resettlement.

Moreover, an imperial grace decree now commands that, for all who accept pacification and return, Le Bao is to summon Subprefect Liu Qing together with Sichuan prefects and magistrates of long-standing clean reputation to deliberate proper resettlement.
Literal English makes returning people the ones ordered to summon Liu Qing; Chinese has Le Bao summon Liu Qing to settle those who return.
Shen Kun argued that sheltering subordinates in Yixing had led to a great case in which many students were swept up and punished;
Shen Kun argued that Yixing sheltered subordinates, which led to a great case in which many students were implicated and punished;
Parallel 論X lines name officials; 宜興 is likewise a personal name here, not the Jiangsu place-name.
Shen Kun argued that in Yixing, sheltering subordinates led to a great case in which many students were implicated and punished;
Shen Kun argued that Yixing sheltered subordinates, leading to a great case in which many students were implicated and punished;
Same referent error: 宜興 is the official criticized, not a locative.

You Guangyi argued that great ministers had not yet achieved full harmony, that military preparations had not yet been fully rectified, and that he wished to emulate Wei Zhengyuan's Ten Reflections memorial to aid good government.

You Guangyi argued that great ministers had not yet achieved full harmony, that military preparations had not yet been fully rectified, and that he wished to emulate Wei Yuancheng's (Wei Zheng's) Ten Reflections memorial to aid good government.
魏元成 is Wei Zheng (魏徵), also known as 元成; 'Zhengyuan' is a mistransliteration.
When Gong Fu saw Songyun punished for opposing the eastern tour, he drafted a secret memorial, settled his affairs, and only then submitted it—and in the end was pardoned.
When Gong Tang saw Songyun punished for opposing the eastern tour, he drafted a secret memorial, settled his affairs, and only then submitted it—and in the end was pardoned.
龔鏜 corresponds to Gong Tang; English 'Gong Fu' does not match 鏜.

Moreover, when Gong Fu saw Songyun punished for remonstrating against the eastern tour, he submitted a secret memorial stating his views again, put his affairs in order for after his death, and only then presented it—ultimately receiving lenient pardon.

Moreover, when Gong Tang saw Songyun punished for remonstrating against the eastern tour, he submitted a secret memorial stating his views again, put his affairs in order for after his death, and only then presented it—ultimately receiving lenient pardon.
Same name error: 鏜 is Tang, not Fu.
